decisions.claim: B has been admitted to study something B really likes
decisions.reason: Second-review support: In the conversational context, Turn 3 asks B about 'news from university,' and Turn 5 responds 'I am glad you can study something you really like!' The presupposition of 'you can study something you really like' in direct response to a question about university news establishes that B has a confirmed pathway to study (most naturally admission). While the initial review notes that 'can study' doesn't strictly entail 'has been admitted,' the discourse context (A just shared admission news, then asked about university news, then expressed gladness about B being able to study) makes admission the only coherent reading. The claim is minimally justified at E2 level.
decisions.counterexample: B could theoretically have gotten a scholarship or already been enrolled, but the question 'Have you got any news from university?' followed by 'I am glad you can study...' strongly implies a new admission result rather than an ongoing status.
